summary: This is revision 1 of 2 of a larger feature (R1 to R5). The left sidebar of Tinkerdeck gains two tabs. Projects keeps what the sidebar shows today (the Home row and each app with its terminals); Files shows the existing file-system explorer filling the panel, so users no longer scroll past every app to reach it. The collapsed rail gains Projects and Files icons that expand the pane straight onto that tab, and selecting an app, terminal, Home or file never switches the tab by itself. The explorer's root rules and the apps/terminals list are unchanged. Naming the app in the Files header, the Projects roll-up status dot, remembering the last tab across restarts and the Ctrl+Shift+E shortcut are revision 2, not this revision.
roles: The person using the app on their own machine: switches between the Projects and Files tabs in the left sidebar to browse apps, terminals and files, and can expand the collapsed rail directly onto either tab.

requirements.text: The expanded left sidebar shows two tabs, Projects and Files, and only the selected tab's content is visible: Projects shows the existing Home row and each app with its terminals; Files shows only the file explorer, filling the sidebar's available height. The sidebar opens on Projects when no tab has been chosen.
requirements.rationale: The explorer currently sits at the bottom of the one scrolling sidebar, so it is pushed further down as apps are added; a tab makes it a direct destination while leaving the project list itself unchanged.
acceptance: Choosing Projects shows the Home row and the app/terminal list and no file explorer.
Choosing Files shows the file explorer and not the Home row or the app/terminal list.
The file explorer is not rendered below the last app or terminal inside the Projects tab.
On first opening the sidebar, before any tab has been chosen, Projects is the selected tab.
edgeCases: A sidebar with no apps still shows both the Projects and Files tabs when the explorer has a folder to show.
The Files tab shows the explorer's existing loading, empty-folder, error and no-folder-hint states unchanged.
When there are no apps and no folder the explorer can root at, the app keeps hiding the sidebar exactly as it does today.
Moving between tabs never restarts a terminal, changes the selected app, or changes the active editor file.
This revision does not remember the tab, so after closing and reopening the app the sidebar starts on Projects again.
pitfalls: The explorer must not remain inside the Projects list at the bottom; that is the placement being removed.
Clicking a tab must not start or stop anything, open a file, or change the selected app.
The existing App component must not be made to own the active tab for this revision; the tab can be chosen and shown inside the sidebar area.

requirements.text: The Projects | Files tab strip stays fixed at the top of the expanded sidebar and remains visible and clickable without vertical scrolling, however many apps and terminals the Projects list contains.
requirements.rationale: The complaint is discoverability: the explorer moves further down with every app, so the tabs must not scroll away with the list.
acceptance: With more apps and terminals than fit in the sidebar, the Files tab is still visible and selectable without scrolling the sidebar.
The tab strip keeps the same position with one app as with many.
Only the selected tab's content scrolls; the tab strip itself does not scroll away.
edgeCases: The tab strip remains visible while the Projects list is scrolled to its bottom.
The tab strip stays inside the sidebar width when the app list is long and names are long.
pitfalls: The tab strip must not be placed inside the scrolling Projects content so that it can scroll away.
The Files tab must stay reachable when the sidebar has hundreds of rows, not just a handful.

requirements.text: The collapsed sidebar rail keeps Expand, Home and the app initials with their status dots, and adds a Projects icon and a Files icon. Clicking the Projects icon expands the pane and selects the Projects tab in one action; clicking the Files icon expands the pane and selects the Files tab in one action. The rail's tab icons use the expand/collapse control the sidebar already receives and choose their tab inside the sidebar area, so this revision needs no new tab state or tab handlers in the app shell.
requirements.rationale: The rail currently has no way into Files, so the two icons close that gap and let the user choose a destination directly. The app shell already passes its expand/collapse control to the sidebar, so the tab can be chosen there; remembering the tab and its shortcut, which do need the app shell, are revision 2.
acceptance: From the collapsed rail, clicking the Projects icon expands the sidebar and shows the Projects tab.
From the collapsed rail, clicking the Files icon expands the sidebar and shows the Files tab.
The collapsed rail still shows Expand, Home and every app initial alongside the two new icons.
Each rail tab click both expands the pane and selects that tab; it never expands onto the previously selected tab.
edgeCases: The rail shows both new icons even when there are no apps.
The rail visibly indicates which tab is active, following the existing rail-active style.
Clicking Home or an app initial in the rail keeps today's behaviour and does not change the active tab.
Both rail icons carry an accessible name and a title.
pitfalls: The new rail icons must not replace Expand, Home or the app initials.
Clicking a rail tab icon must expand and select its tab together, never one without the other.

Do not add the active-tab state or the rail tab handlers to the old app shell (src/App.tsx) for this revision; the sidebar already receives the expand/collapse callback, and a later revision, not this one, is what needs the app shell for remembering the tab and its shortcut.
The old Sidebar prop comment saying the explorer is never in the rail, and the test asserting the rail never shows Files, must be updated to the new behaviour rather than left contradicting it.

requirements.text: Selecting an app, a terminal, Home or a file never changes the active sidebar tab by itself; in this revision the tab changes only when the user clicks a tab or clicks a rail tab icon.
requirements.rationale: Losing the Files tree because a file was opened, or losing Projects because a terminal was started, would fight the user's explicit choice.
acceptance: With Files active, opening a file from the explorer leaves the sidebar on Files.
With Projects active, selecting an app or terminal leaves the sidebar on Projects.
With Files active, a new file tab opening in the editor leaves the sidebar on Files.
edgeCases: A file operation that closes or re-points an editor tab does not switch the sidebar tab.
Choosing Home from the palette or the sidebar does not switch the tab.
pitfalls: Do not tie the active tab to the current view (home/app/editor), the selected app, or the active editor file.

requirements.text: The tab strip is operable by keyboard and assistive technology: it exposes a tab list with two tabs and a tab panel, marks the selected tab, gives each tab a text label, shows a visible focus, and supports Left/Right arrow keys between the tabs.
requirements.rationale: A tab strip that works only with a mouse excludes people, and a control that does not announce which tab is selected is confusing to screen-reader users.
acceptance: A screen reader announces a tab list with Projects and Files and which one is selected.
Tab moves focus into the tab strip, Left/Right arrow keys move between the two tabs and select them, and Enter or Space also selects the focused tab.
The focused tab has a clearly visible focus ring.
edgeCases: The selected tab is conveyed by more than colour: it is announced and visually distinct.
Both tab labels stay legible and clickable when the sidebar is at its narrowest, without horizontal scrolling.
pitfalls: Do not implement the tabs as plain buttons with no announced selected state.
Do not rely on colour alone to show the selected tab.

outOfScope: Naming the app (or Misc/Home) in the Files header - revision 2
The roll-up status dot on the Projects tab label - revision 2
Remembering the last tab across restarts - revision 2
The Ctrl+Shift+E shortcut for the Files tab - revision 2
Changing which root folder the file-system explorer shows (src/features/explorer/root.ts stays as it is)
Adding, renaming, moving or deleting files from the sidebar
A split view with a draggable or resizable divider between Projects and Files

nonFunctional.statement: The Projects | Files tab strip can be used with the keyboard alone and is announced correctly by a screen reader.
nonFunctional.acceptance: With focus in the sidebar, Tab reaches the tab strip, Left/Right change the selected tab, the selected tab is announced, and the focus ring is visible.

nonFunctional.statement: Switching between Projects and Files stays responsive with a long project list (up to 50 apps with up to 10 terminals each).
nonFunctional.acceptance: With 50 apps and 500 terminals, a tab switch completes within 100 ms on the developer's machine, the tab strip stays in place, and scrolling the Projects list shows no visible freeze.

risks: While Files is open the per-app status dots are out of sight, so users lose status at a glance; the roll-up dot on the Projects label is revision 2.
With projects hidden, users may not know which app's folder the explorer is showing; naming it in the Files header is revision 2.
Existing tests look for the Files region directly and assume it always renders; they must select the Files tab first, or assert the new default, or they will fail for the wrong reason.
glossary: Projects tab: the sidebar tab listing the Home row and each app with its terminals.
Files tab: the sidebar tab hosting the file-system explorer.
File-system explorer: the tree of folders and files rooted at the selected app, the app owning the active editor tab, a Misc file's folder, or Home.
Collapsed rail: the narrow sidebar showing Expand, Home, the app initials, and the Projects and Files icons.

coverage.note: The developer described the person using the app on their own machine, who browses apps, terminals and files; there is only this one local role.
Revision 1 only reorganises existing sidebar content and stores no new data; remembering the last tab is revision 2.
Local single-user app; the tabs expose the same projects and files the user can already access, and no new access rules are needed.
No data entry in this change, so there is no invalid input to handle.
The Files tab reuses the explorer's existing loading, empty-folder, error and no-folder-hint states unchanged; the Projects tab keeps today's empty-app behaviour.
No records are created, so double submit and duplicates do not apply.
Assumed up to 50 apps with 10 terminals each (500 rows); the tab strip stays visible and switching stays responsive.
Nothing is deleted by this change.
The explorer shows the same files that are already visible today; no new personal or sensitive data is introduced.
The feature request itself specifies accessible tabs (tablist/tab/tabpanel, aria-selected, keyboard), and the stack guidance gives the performance default.

assumptions: The Files tab shows whatever state the explorer already shows (loading, empty folder, error, or a hint when no folder can be rooted); revision 1 adds no new states.
The sidebar is expected to stay usable with up to 50 apps and 10 terminals each (500 rows).
